result: Root cause: no Ziv fast tier in most families (dd path on every call, 384-bit mp on every special/long double call, software division and per-call constants in mp); CR is a decision, not a spec requirement; report + 7 redesign briefs

rulings.item: R1 accuracy contract per family (CR everywhere vs ulp bound for lgamma/tgamma/Bessel/x87)
rulings.recommendation: A: keep CR, build Ziv fast tiers; record residuals for lgamma/tgamma/Bessel/x87; switch a family to a ulp bound only if it stays above ~2x in time after its fast tier

rulings.item: R2 parity yardstick for x87 long double rows
rulings.recommendation: measure in cycles/ns on a booked timing host; instruction counts compare against single microcoded x87 instructions

informational: the reference is not correctly rounded on any measured function (differs on 0.01-54% of inputs, up to 4 ulp; j0 791 ulp)
elem.rs states the f64 double-double path is CR except within ~2^-100 of a boundary: D-10.13's 'every result correctly rounded' is not proved for double
mp::ln10() recomputes ln 10 by series per call (log10l ~2x avoidable)
improvement: a fastpath-stats + perf harness for libm per-path costs belongs in validation/ so tuning stories stop re-deriving it
next_step: rule R1/R2; dispatch LIBM-MP-CORE-SPEED first, then the F64/F32 kernel briefs
